activity_context.topic_title: The Divergence of a Vector Field

feedback.problem:
Consider the vector field $F=x{e}^{y}\,i+xy{e}^{y}\,j.$ 
Evaluate $∇\cdot F$ at the point $(2,0).$
feedback.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the divergence of $F$ is the scalar field given by

$$
∇\cdot F=\text{div}\,F=\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}.
$$

  

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{e}^{y})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy{e}^{y}) \\  & ={e}^{y}+x{e}^{y}+xy{e}^{y}. \\  & =(1+x+xy){e}^{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate $\text{div}\,F$ at the point $(2,0),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\cdot F)(2,0) & =(1+2+2(0)){e}^{0} \\  & =3{e}^{0} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
